rows.evidence: Q1: Sections 2.1-2.3 - two-year (2019-2020) split-plot field experiment in Tongliao with SI vs under-mulch drip (MI) at three irrigation levels, soil sampled at 0-20 and 20-40 cm and sequenced (16S, ITS). Q2: Section 3.1/Fig. 2 and Section 3.4/Fig. 6 - bacterial OTU numbers in 0-20 cm higher under SI than MI; LEfSe shows Holophagae, Thermoanaerobaculaceae, Microtrichales, Solirubrobacterales, Myxococcales enriched in SI1 (0-20 cm); Section 4 and Conclusion state SI topsoil is a relatively fertile habitat for beneficial microorganisms, whereas MI enriched microplastic-degrading Nocardioidaceae.
rows.notes: Study supports the enrichment-of-beneficial-microorganisms part of the claim for SI relative to under-mulch drip; the 'no plastic pollution' point is inherent in the SI design (no film) rather than measured, and economic/ecological benefits (extension area, groundwater decline, yield/economic gains) are cited from other work (Mengxi 2020, Jianglu 2022, Haiyun 2021), not measured here. Q3: single method (amplicon sequencing); soil N measurements used only for correlation. Q4: soil moisture/temperature mechanism is asserted from literature, not measured; nutrient correlations (RDA, Fig. 8) are associations, not a demonstrated intermediate pathway. Q5/Q6: one site, one crop, 120 m2 plots. Q7: effect differs by irrigation level (significant at 50%) but not stated as a requirement. Q8: no limitations stated. Q9: Table 4 gives means with letter groupings only; no SD/CI reported; alpha-diversity indices mostly not significantly different between SI and MI. 'Beneficial' functions of enriched taxa are inferred from cited literature.

notes: Full text appears complete. Note Table 1 irrigation amounts appear mislabeled relative to treatment names (SI40 listed with 1800 m3/ha), but this does not affect the rating.
